outcome: Since 26 January 2024 no source I could open shows a proof, disproof or formal verification of Beilinson's conjectures on special values of L-functions. The in-window activity is partial: numerical checks of the L-value/regulator identity for particular curves and motives, unconditional nontriviality of regulators for constructed classes, conditional reductions in neighbouring Bloch–Kato and Beilinson–Bloch settings, an Albanese-kernel case of a conjecture the author also calls Beilinson's, and a 1 August 2026 preprint on Boyd's Mahler-measure identities whose authors disclose that Claude and Axolver were used for data analysis and neural-network experiments.
problem_asks: The bullet is 'Beilinson's conjectures about special values of L-functions' (linked to the Wikipedia article 'Special values of L-functions'; Analytic number theory subsection). Parts: (a) for a smooth projective variety X over a number field, the Beilinson regulator from motivic cohomology / algebraic K-groups of X to real Deligne cohomology is an isomorphism after realification, so that the real Deligne cohomology carries a rational structure; (b) the first non-zero Taylor coefficient of the L-function of X at each integer point s is, up to a non-zero rational number, the determinant comparing the two rational structures (the regulator determinant); (c) this holds for all such varieties and all integer points in the range the conjecture covers, not only special families, critical values or single cases; (d) the rational number is left unspecified ('up to a non-zero rational number'), so a result that fixes or computes it bears on (b) without being an instance of (a)-(c) as such. The bullet mentions no Chow groups, Albanese kernels, Beilinson–Soulé vanishing or Beilinson–Bloch–Kato Selmer statements; those are separate conjectures in the Beilinson circle, recorded below as neighbours.

events.what_happened: François Brunault and Masataka Chida, 'Regulators for Rankin–Selberg products of modular forms', arXiv:1503.04626 (March 2015 per the arXiv identifier; not opened). Per the search summary, it proves a weak version of Beilinson's conjecture for non-critical values of Rankin–Selberg L-functions of two modular forms, under a nonvanishing hypothesis on an automorphic factor and a restriction on levels or weights.
events.delivers: A weak (non-critical) form of the regulator identity for Rankin–Selberg products of two modular forms, under the stated nonvanishing hypothesis. Context only; read from a search summary, not the paper.
events.remains: The general conjecture for all varieties and integer points; the critical values; the full regulator isomorphism.
events.direction: Partial special case, consistent with the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Evangelia Gazaki and Jonathan R. Love, 'Hyperelliptic curves mapping to abelian varieties and applications to Beilinson's conjecture for zero-cycles', arXiv:2309.06361 (v1 12 Sep 2023; v2 4 Nov 2023; v3 9 Mar 2026; 32 pages). For abelian surfaces A isogenous to a product of elliptic curves, they build a large family of pairwise non-isomorphic hyperelliptic curves mapping birationally into A (infinitely many of genus g for infinitely many g), use them to find many rational equivalences in CH_0(A), and claim 'some progress' toward Beilinson's conjecture for zero-cycles (the Albanese kernel of a smooth projective variety over the algebraic closure of Q is zero).
events.revisions: v2 4 Nov 2023; v3 9 Mar 2026. The search summary says v1 framed the result differently; I did not check v1's text.
events.delivers: Rational equivalences in CH_0(A) for abelian surfaces isogenous to a product of elliptic curves, i.e. partial progress on Albanese-kernel vanishing for that class of surfaces. Does not reach surfaces outside the class and says nothing about L-values or regulators.
events.remains: Albanese-kernel vanishing for all smooth projective varieties over the algebraic closure of Q, and the L-value/regulator form of Beilinson's conjecture.
events.time_since_posted: 37 months from v1; 7 months from v3
events.direction: Partial progress on the zero-cycle/Albanese-kernel form for a restricted class of abelian surfaces; consistent with the conjecture it targets.
events.object: A family of hyperelliptic curves mapping birationally into each such abelian surface, explicit in construction; the rational equivalences come from the resulting relations in CH_0(A). Not a counterexample to anything.

events.what_happened: Quentin Gazda, 'Regulators in the Arithmetic of Function Fields', arXiv:2207.03461 (v1 7 Jul 2022; v3 18 Feb 2026). Defines a regulator for rigid analytically trivial Anderson A-motives over function fields, follows the number-field picture via the Hodge–Pink realization, proves a finiteness result for A-motivic cohomology, shows equal dimension of source and target under a weight assumption, and reports that the regulator's image may fail to have full rank, which would block an analogue of Beilinson's conjecture in that setting. The author says conjecture (III) is to be addressed in later work. Seen in a search summary; not opened.
events.delivers: Function-field analogue only: a regulator for Anderson motives, a finiteness result, a dimension count under a weight assumption, and a negative finding that the image may not have full rank. Not the number-field statement.
events.remains: The number-field conjecture in the bullet is untouched.
events.time_since_posted: 51 months from v1; 8 months from v3
events.direction: Negative finding for a function-field analogue only; discounted as a different question.

events.what_happened: François Brunault, 'On the K_4 group of modular curves', arXiv:2009.07614 (v1 16 Sep 2020; v2 19 Sep 2022; v3 29 Aug 2025, described by the author as a significant revision). Constructs elements of K_4 of modular curves from weight-3 polylogarithmic complexes using new modular units (cross-ratios of division values of the Weierstrass ℘-function). Conjectures that these elements are proportional to the Beilinson elements defined via Eisenstein symbols, supported by numerical computations and results of Wang.
events.revisions: v2 19 Sep 2022; v3 29 Aug 2025 (rewritten introduction, restructured paper, 'some mathematical improvements').
events.delivers: Explicit construction of K_4 elements on modular curves. The proportionality to Beilinson elements is conjectured, not proved. This is within Beilinson's Eisenstein-symbol programme but is not an L-value identity.
events.remains: The proportionality (conjectural) and the L-value/regulator statement of the bullet.
events.time_since_posted: 73 months from v1; 14 months from v3
events.doubts: The proportionality to the Beilinson elements rests on numerical computations and on results of Wang; the abstract states it as a conjecture.
events.direction: Constructive; the link to the Beilinson elements is conjectural. No bearing on whether the bullet is proved.
events.object: Explicit K_4 elements of modular curves, given by cross-ratios of division values of ℘ and weight-3 polylogarithmic complexes. Explicit, not existence-only.

events.what_happened: François Brunault, Rob de Jeu, Hang Liu and Fernando Rodriguez Villegas, 'K_2 of families of elliptic curves over non-Abelian cubic and quartic fields', arXiv:2401.04510 (v1 9 Jan 2024; the only version listed at capture). Gives two constructions of elliptic-curve families over cubic and quartic fields, each yielding integral elements in the kernel of the tame symbol in K_2 (linearly independent; fields generally non-abelian), a new integrality criterion, and a numerical verification of Beilinson's conjecture for K_2 for 'just over 90' curves (abstract) or 93 curves (introduction).
events.delivers: Numerical support for Beilinson's K_2 regulator identity for about 90 to 93 explicitly constructed elliptic curves over cubic and quartic fields, and integrality of the constructed K_2 elements. Restricted to those families; the identity is verified numerically for these curves, not proved.
events.remains: Beilinson's K_2 conjecture for all other curves and fields, and the general L-value/regulator statement.
events.directly_checkable: The curves are explicit and the L-values and regulators can be recomputed from the paper's data; I did not recompute them.
events.doubts: Numerical verification only. The abstract says 'just over 90' curves and the introduction says 93; the precision is stated in Section 7, which I could not read.
events.direction: Consistent with Beilinson's K_2 conjecture for the curves checked; no counter-instance reported.
events.object: Integral elements of K_2 of elliptic curves over cubic and quartic fields, built explicitly and compared numerically with L-values; the numerical comparison is the verification.

events.what_happened: Vasily Golyshev and Matt Kerr, 'The arithmetic of Calabi–Yau motives and mobile higher regulators', arXiv:2409.19549 (MPIM-Bonn-2024; v1 29 Sep 2024; v2 13 Dec 2024). Constructs elements of the motivic cohomology of rank-4, weight-3 Calabi–Yau motives in hypergeometric families (cases p=3 and p=4), computes their regulators explicitly, and realises Hodge classes by cycles, which the authors say proves Beilinson's Hodge-type conjecture in these cases. Reports the first numerical checks of Beilinson's conjectures on special values of L-functions for such motives; in the readable introduction the numerical evidence is that L'(M_t,0)/r(t) and L''(M_t,0)/r(t) are rational for suitable rational t.
events.delivers: For the rank-4, weight-3 Calabi–Yau motives of the p=3 and p=4 families: non-trivial motivic classes with explicit regulators; cycles realising Hodge classes (a Beilinson–Hodge-type statement, per the authors); and numerical evidence, not proof, that the L-value ratios are rational for suitable rational t. Restricted to those families.
events.remains: The L-value/regulator identity for all such motives and all integer points, with the rational factors proved rather than observed.
events.doubts: The numerical L-value checks are the only evidence for the L-value part. Sections 8 and 10, where precision and method would be given, were not readable.
events.direction: Numerical evidence consistent with the L-value/regulator relation for the motives studied; the Hodge-class realisation is a proved statement in these cases.
events.object: Motivic cohomology classes and cycles built from hypergeometric families of rank-4, weight-3 Calabi–Yau motives, with regulators given through the hypergeometric data. Built explicitly; not existence-only.

events.what_happened: Frédéric Déglise, 'Generic motives and motivic cohomology of fields', arXiv:2408.06233 (v1 12 Aug 2024; v2 11 Jan 2025; v3 20 Jul 2025). Studies generic motives and motivic cohomology of fields; proposes a conjecture complementing the Beilinson–Soulé vanishing conjecture; gives a direct argument for the weights in the λ-structure of the K-theory of number fields that avoids regulator maps; proves that motivic cohomology of R and C is uncountable in many bidegrees.
events.revisions: v2 11 Jan 2025; v3 20 Jul 2025 (rewritten introduction, historical background, appendix on infinity-categories).
events.delivers: Not an instance of the bullet's statement. It concerns the Beilinson–Soulé vanishing conjecture, a different Beilinson conjecture about motivic cohomology. The abstract proposes a complementing conjecture rather than proving Beilinson–Soulé, and gives a direct argument for the λ-structure weights.
events.remains: The bullet's L-value/regulator statement is untouched.
events.direction: Neighbour only. No bearing on the regulator/L-value statement.

events.what_happened: Giada Grossi, David Loeffler and Sarah Livia Zerbes, 'Asai-Flach classes, p-adic L-functions and the Bloch–Kato conjecture for GO(4)', arXiv:2407.17055 (v1 24 Jul 2024, under the earlier title 'On the Bloch-Kato conjecture and Iwasawa main conjecture for GO(4)'; v2 17 Feb 2025). Proves the Bloch–Kato conjecture for critical values of Asai L-functions of p-ordinary Hilbert modular forms over quadratic fields with p split; one inclusion in the Iwasawa main conjecture for these L-functions up to a power of p; and a p-adic Eichler–Shimura comparison isomorphism for Hida families.
events.revisions: v2 17 Feb 2025 (merges v1 with arXiv:2309.07536, per the arXiv page).
events.delivers: A Bloch–Kato (Selmer/Galois-cohomology) statement for critical Asai values, for quadratic-field Hilbert forms with p split. It is not a regulator identity. The abstract page does not mention Beilinson's conjecture.
events.remains: Beilinson's regulator statement; Bloch–Kato outside this range (non-split p, other Asai values).
events.direction: Proves Bloch–Kato in its range; a neighbour to the bullet, not a regulator identity.

events.what_happened: Yusuke Nemoto and Takuya Yamauchi, 'Regulators on some abelian coverings of P¹ minus n+2 points', arXiv:2512.24607 (v1 31 Dec 2025; 16 pages; math.NT and math.AG). Constructs rational or integral elements of the motivic cohomology of superelliptic curves that are quotients of abelian coverings of P¹ minus n+2 points; shows they are non-trivial by expressing their regulators through Appell–Lauricella hypergeometric functions; checks integrality under a mild assumption; gives numerical examples for Beilinson's conjecture on special values of L-functions of superelliptic curves (elliptic curves over Q, a genus-2 hyperelliptic curve, a genus-3 superelliptic curve).
events.delivers: Non-triviality of certain motivic cohomology classes on superelliptic curves of this family (non-zero regulators). Integrality of these classes holds only under a 'mild assumption' that the abstract does not state. Numerical agreement with the conjecture for a few named curves. Restricted to the superelliptic family.
events.remains: The conjecture for all varieties and integer points; integrality without the assumption; the L-value identity beyond the listed examples.
events.doubts: Integrality is conditional on an assumption the abstract does not state. The numerical checks are the only evidence for the L-value part. No journal version listed.
events.direction: Non-triviality of regulators supports the existence of regulator classes in the family; the numerical checks are consistent with the conjecture.
events.object: Motivic cohomology classes on superelliptic curves whose regulators are given by Appell–Lauricella hypergeometric integrals. Built explicitly; non-triviality is shown by computing the regulator.

events.what_happened: Kalyan Banerjee, 'Beilinson's conjecture on K3 surfaces with an involution', arXiv:2502.09380 (single author; v1 13 Feb 2025; v2 5 Mar 2026, 'certain clarifications in the arguments are added'). Theorem 1.1: for a K3 surface S over the algebraic closure of Q with an involution i such that S/i is the projective plane branched along a sextic, if S contains infinitely many rational curves then 'Beilinson's conjecture holds on S'. The argument shows that the degree-zero Chow group A_0(S) is zero, via finite-dimensionality in the sense of Roitman and the action of i_* (Theorems 2.6 to 2.8). Remark 2.10 notes that Theorem 2.2 uses Faltings' result and does not apply over C.
events.revisions: v2 5 Mar 2026: 'certain clarifications in the arguments are added' (12 pages).
events.delivers: A_0(S) = 0 for the stated class of K3 surfaces over the algebraic closure of Q: the Albanese-kernel form of Beilinson's conjecture, which the paper calls 'Beilinson's conjecture' for these surfaces. It involves no L-values and no regulators. Restricted to surfaces meeting all the hypotheses (involution, quotient P^2, sextic branch locus, infinitely many rational curves).
events.remains: All other K3 surfaces and varieties; the L-value/regulator form of Beilinson's conjecture that the bullet's wording describes.
events.time_since_posted: 20 months from v1; 7 months from v2
events.doubts: Single author. The result depends on infinitely many rational curves on S and on Faltings' result (Remark 2.10 says it does not apply over C). Only the v2 clarifications are noted; no journal reference or review was found in the searches run.
events.direction: Affirms the Albanese-kernel form for the stated surfaces. Silent on L-values.

events.what_happened: Matt Broe, 'On the Beilinson–Bloch conjecture over function fields', arXiv:2505.00696 (v1 1 May 2025; v2 27 Jan 2026). Gives a criterion (Theorem 1.1) for the Beilinson–Bloch conjecture in codimension i for a smooth projective X over a global function field K, extending a result of Jannsen: the base-changed cycle class map must be an isomorphism after tensoring with Q and the eigenvalue-1 part of Frobenius must be semisimple. Also a new proof of a theorem of Geisser; the Tate conjecture for products of a smooth projective curve with a power of a CM elliptic curve over any finitely generated field, with special cases of Beilinson–Bloch deduced; and a conditional answer to a question of Moonen on Chow groups.
events.delivers: Beilinson–Bloch for X_K under hypotheses (1) to (3) of Theorem 1.1, which is an implication and not unconditional by itself. Unconditional: Theorem 1.4 (Tate conjecture for E^g × C) and Theorem 1.5 (vanishing of certain Chow groups of tensor powers of h^1(E) over a global function field), which together give Beilinson–Bloch for powers of a CM elliptic curve over a global function field. Geisser's equivalences are unconditional; the Tate–Shafarevich order formula is conditional. Corollary 6.14 is conditional.
events.remains: Beilinson–Bloch for number fields and for general varieties over function fields; the bullet's regulator/L-value statement, which Beilinson–Bloch (Chow groups against order of vanishing of L-functions) does not state.
events.time_since_posted: 17 months from v1; 8 months from v2
events.doubts: Corollary 6.14 is conditional on agreement of rational and homological equivalence up to torsion over F_p. The criterion needs its hypotheses verified for each variety. No journal version listed.
events.direction: A function-field analogue of Beilinson–Bloch, with unconditional special cases. Analogue, not the number-field statement.

events.what_happened: Chan-Ho Kim and Robert Pollack, arXiv:2505.09121 (v1 14 May 2025; no later version listed). The arXiv page gives the title 'The refined Tamagawa number conjectures for GL₂'; the search summary described the same ID as a refined Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer-type formula. Proves a refined formula for Bloch–Kato Selmer groups of the central critical twist of a cuspidal newform at ordinary primes p ≥ 3 with large image, using Kolyvagin derivatives and assuming the Iwasawa main conjecture localised at the augmentation ideal. Consequences include non-vanishing of Kato's Kolyvagin system, a p-converse to Gross–Zagier and Kolyvagin, the p-parity conjecture and a new upper bound on Selmer ranks. Per the abstract, it also completes a 'discrete' analogue of the Beilinson–Bloch–Kato conjecture for modular forms at ordinary primes.
events.delivers: For GL_2 modular forms at ordinary primes with large image, under the localised Iwasawa main conjecture hypothesis: a refined Selmer formula and its consequences. The 'discrete analogue' is a Selmer-side statement, not the regulator/L-value identity.
events.remains: The regulator/L-value identity; the cases without the Iwasawa hypothesis; non-ordinary primes.
events.doubts: Conditional on the localised Iwasawa main conjecture. The appendix has numerical examples. Only the abstract page was read.
events.direction: Conditional Selmer-side formula and a discrete analogue of Beilinson–Bloch–Kato. Neighbour, not the bullet's statement.

events.what_happened: Hao Peng, 'On the Beilinson–Bloch–Kato conjecture for polarized motives', arXiv:2509.18615 (single version; 23 Sep 2025; 59 pages). In the conjugate self-dual case: if the central L-value does not vanish, the associated Bloch–Kato Selmer group with coefficients in a suitable local field vanishes. In the self-dual analytic rank-zero case: reduces the conjecture to an endoscopic Rankin–Selberg conjecture about orthogonal Gross–Prasad periods.
events.delivers: In the conjugate self-dual case, non-vanishing of the central L-value implies vanishing of the Bloch–Kato Selmer group (the only hypothesis named in the abstract). The self-dual rank-zero case is a reduction to a companion conjecture, not a proof. The abstract does not mention Beilinson's regulator conjecture.
events.remains: The rank-zero case (reduced to the Gross–Prasad companion); the regulator/L-value statement of the bullet.
events.doubts: The rank-zero case depends on the companion conjecture. Only the abstract was read; the PDF was not readable beyond its outline, so the exact hypotheses are unverified.
events.direction: Consistent with the Beilinson–Bloch–Kato framework; partial unconditional result in one case and a conditional reduction in another. Neighbour, not the bullet's statement.

events.what_happened: Neil Dummigan, Vasily Golyshev, Rob de Jeu and Matt Kerr, 'The 2-part of the Bloch–Kato conjecture, and indivisibility results, for K_2 of some elliptic curves', arXiv:2605.11100 (v1 11 May 2026; math.NT, math.AG, math.KT). For the curves E_u: y² = x(x+1)(x+u²), a twisted Legendre family 2-isogenous to a family studied by Boyd, and for certain integers u: studies the 2-part of the Bloch–Kato conjecture for L(E_u,2); constructs an element of the integral kernel of the tame symbol on K_2 of an integral model with non-vanishing regulator and proves it is not 2-divisible modulo torsion, using the Merkurjev–Suslin norm residue isomorphism; numerically tests the 2-part in many cases. Section 3 states Beilinson's conjecture in determinant form and says Bloch–Kato is what fixes the rational factor up to which L(E_u,2) is determined by the regulator.
events.delivers: For the family E_u and certain integers u: the 2-part of the Bloch–Kato conjecture for L(E_u,2) in the authors' sense, and an indivisibility result for a K_2 element. Their Section 3 identifies Bloch–Kato as what fixes the rational factor in Beilinson's identity, so this concerns that factor's 2-adic part for these curves (a reading of the text, not a quoted sentence). Restricted to the family and to the 2-part; odd parts and other curves are untouched.
events.remains: The odd part of the rational factor; all other curves; Beilinson's identity itself; Bloch–Kato in general.
events.directly_checkable: The element α_u and the curves E_u are explicit, and the authors give numerical 2-adic tests. I did not recompute them.
events.doubts: Proof is for the indivisibility; the 2-part of Bloch–Kato is supported by numerical tests in many cases, not proved in full. Parts of the paper after Section 3 were not readable.
events.direction: Consistent with Beilinson and Bloch–Kato. Proves indivisibility and the 2-part for a restricted family; numerical evidence elsewhere.
events.object: An explicit element α_u of the integral kernel of the tame symbol on K_2 of an integral model of E_u (for u ≡ 4 mod 8, with conditions), with non-vanishing regulator, shown not to be divisible by 2^(m_u) modulo torsion. Explicit construction; the indivisibility is proved.

events.what_happened: Alberto Alfarano, Pablo Bianucci, Matilde N. Lalín and Berend Ringeling, 'Machine learning the arithmetic of Boyd's Mahler measure conjectures', arXiv:2608.00615 (v1 1 Aug 2026; 36 pages, 19 figures; math.NT). For Boyd's family P_k = x + y + 1/x + 1/y + k, Boyd observed numerically that m(P_k) = r_k · L'(E_k,0) with r_k rational. The paper uses data for the first 250,000 values of k. It recovers Boyd's observation that, apart from a few exceptions, r_k is the reciprocal of an integer; reports p-adic valuation distributions (for p ≥ 5, the probability of v_p(r_k) = -m appears to be p^(-m)); reports 3-adic parity laws and a 2-adic negative-binomial heuristic, which the authors call 'a heuristic observation rather than a precise conjecture'; proves Lemma 3.1 (bounds on L(E,2)); gives a conditional proof of Conjecture 3.2 for k = 4u (Proposition 3.4) assuming Bloch–Kato and other hypotheses from Dummigan–Golyshev–de Jeu–Kerr; and reports transformer-based neural-network experiments using Axolver and statistical analysis assisted by Claude. Beilinson's conjecture is cited as motivation (following Deninger, Boyd and Rodriguez-Villegas); the paper does not claim to prove or refute it.
events.delivers: Observed (numerical and machine-learning) arithmetic of the rational factors r_k in Boyd's identities for the family P_k; one proved lemma; and a conditional result (Proposition 3.4) on the 2-adic part for k = 4u under Bloch–Kato and other hypotheses. The L-value identity m(P_k) = r_k · L'(E_k,0) is observed, not proved, for each k. Beilinson's rational factor is the quantity this paper studies: the conjecture asserts proportionality up to a rational number and leaves that number unspecified.
events.remains: The identity m(P_k) = r_k · L'(E_k,0) for all k; Conjecture 3.2 for k not of the form 4u; the Beilinson conjecture itself.
events.directly_checkable: The Mahler measures and L'(E_k,0) for the family can be computed numerically for any given k. I did not recompute them.
events.doubts: The machine-learning results and the observed patterns are not proofs. The proved part is conditional. The authors call the 2-adic negative-binomial model 'a heuristic observation rather than a precise conjecture' (HTML text). The authors' own Declaration says they reviewed and verified all AI outputs.
events.direction: Observations consistent with Boyd's identities, which are Beilinson-type predictions. No counter-instance reported. The conditional result concerns the 2-adic part of r_k.
events.object: The rational numbers r_k for the family P_k, with the reciprocal-integer structure presented as observation. Conjecture 3.2 is stated as a bound and is not proved outside k = 4u. No counterexample is claimed.

systems.name: Claude
systems.what_it_did: Data processing and analysis. The Declaration says Claude was used 'to process, clean, and identify patterns within the research dataset'; the abstract says the statistical analysis was 'assisted by Claude'. The paper does not say which patterns Claude identified, and does not say Claude produced any conjecture, proof or code. The Declaration says the research framework, data collection and final interpretations were 'entirely conceptualized and directed by the human authors'. Access to Claude Max was provided by Anthropic (acknowledgements). The Declaration names it 'Anthropic’s Claude model'.
systems.basis_quote: Anthropic’s Claude model was utilized to process, clean, and identify patterns within the research dataset.

systems.name: Axolver
systems.what_it_did: Trained transformer-based sequence-to-sequence neural networks on the Boyd data (section 4 gives 4 encoder and 4 decoder layers, 8 attention heads). The abstract says the networks 'do not predict r_k exactly' but 'recover significant information about its magnitude and valuations'. The Declaration describes Axolver as a framework from Axiom used to train the networks on mathematical and symbolic reasoning tasks. The paper does not claim the networks produced a theorem or a formula. Axolver is a framework, not a named model.
systems.basis_quote: Axiom’s Axolver framework was used to train sequence-to-sequence neural networks

ai.disclosed_cost: Access to Claude Max was provided by Anthropic during the CRM workshop (acknowledgements). No token, compute or money figures were found in the text read.

events.what_happened: François Brunault, David T.-B. G. Lilienfeldt and Yusuke Nemoto, 'Elements in K_4 and regulator maps of Fermat curves', arXiv:2606.24532 (v1 23 Jun 2026; 40 pages; math.NT, math.AG, math.KT). Constructs explicit elements of K_4^(3) of the Fermat curves x^N + y^N = 1 for every N ≥ 3, using polylogarithmic complexes and de Jeu's map to K-theory; proves they are non-trivial by showing that their images under Beilinson's regulator are non-zero; gives explicit regulator integrals in terms of special values of Zagier's trilogarithm, with the corollary that these integrals are asymptotic to (3/2)ζ(3)N² as N → ∞; derives hypergeometric formulas; and numerically verifies some cases of Beilinson's conjectures at s = 3 for N ∈ {3, 4, 6}, with PARI/GP agreement to at least 35 digits (section 1.2).
events.delivers: Non-triviality of the regulators of explicit K_4^(3) elements for every Fermat curve, which is a regulator-nonvanishing statement for a family. Numerical agreement at s = 3 for three Fermat curves (N = 3, 4, 6), to at least 35 digits per the authors. Restricted to Fermat curves and to s = 3.
events.remains: Beilinson's conjecture for general varieties and integer points; the other values of N; the rational factor for N ≥ 7 and for s other than 3.
events.directly_checkable: The Fermat curves and the trilogarithm integrals are explicit. The numerical checks are reproducible with PARI/GP per the paper; I did not reproduce them.
events.doubts: Numerical checks for three curves only. Not refereed; the paper says 'comments welcome'.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture; non-triviality of regulators; numerical agreement for three Fermat curves.
events.object: Explicit elements of K_4^(3) of the Fermat curves x^N + y^N = 1 (N ≥ 3), built from polylogarithmic complexes, whose regulators are explicit trilogarithm integrals. Explicit construction.

events.what_happened: Thu Ha Trieu, 'The Mahler measure of exact polynomials in three variables', arXiv:2310.06563 (v1 10 Oct 2023; v2 11 Oct 2023; v3 1 Jan 2024; v4 5 Apr 2024; v5 14 Mar 2025). Published in Algebra & Number Theory 20:3 (2026), pp. 525–576, DOI 10.2140/ant.2026.20.525. Proves that under explicit conditions the Mahler measure of a three-variable polynomial can be expressed through elliptic-curve L-values and Bloch–Wigner dilogarithm values, conditionally on Beilinson's conjecture; in some cases the dilogarithm values reduce to Dirichlet L-values. The proof constructs an element of K_4^(3) of a smooth projective curve over a number field. Applied to several Mahler-measure identities conjectured by Boyd and Brunault.
events.revisions: v2 11 Oct 2023; v3 1 Jan 2024; v4 5 Apr 2024; v5 14 Mar 2025. Journal publication: Algebra & Number Theory 20:3 (2026), 525–576.
events.delivers: Conditional identities: for three-variable polynomials satisfying explicit conditions, Mahler measure equals a combination of elliptic-curve L-values and Bloch–Wigner values, up to a rational factor, conditionally on Beilinson's conjecture. Uses the conjecture as a hypothesis; does not establish any instance unconditionally.
events.remains: All of Beilinson's conjecture (it is a hypothesis here); the unconditional status of every identity it applies to.

checked_by.qualification: Refereed journal of record for the published version
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper in volume 20, number 3 (2026). The refereeing itself was not seen; the publication is the evidence.

events.time_since_posted: 36 months from v1; 19 months from v5
events.directly_checkable: The identities are stated for explicit polynomials and can be checked numerically. Not checked here.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture's shape; uses it as a hypothesis, so it neither confirms nor refutes it.

disputes.summary: Two different statements are both called 'Beilinson's conjecture' in 2023–2026 sources. The bullet's wording is the L-value/regulator conjecture ('special values of L-functions'). Banerjee (arXiv 2502.09380) and Gazaki–Love (arXiv 2309.06361) use the name for the Albanese-kernel / zero-cycle statement, which contains no L-values. Whether a restricted case of the second counts toward the bullet is a scope call for the judging pass.

summary: Searches found no proof, disproof or formal verification of Beilinson's conjectures on special values of L-functions in any source I could open, dated after 26 January 2024. The Wikipedia article linked from the bullet (Special values of L-functions, last edited 30 August 2026, so not the frozen revision) says all of the conjectures 'are known to be true only in special cases'. Within the window the sources show the following. (i) Numerical checks of the L-value/regulator identity for particular curves or motives: Golyshev–Kerr (arXiv 2409.19549, Sep 2024), Nemoto–Yamauchi (2512.24607, Dec 2025), Brunault–Lilienfeldt–Nemoto (2606.24532, Jun 2026). The de Jeu et al. K_2 checks (2401.04510) are dated 9 Jan 2024, before the freeze, and are recorded anyway. (ii) Unconditional non-triviality of regulators for constructed classes, in the Nemoto–Yamauchi and Brunault–Lilienfeldt–Nemoto families. (iii) An Albanese-kernel case of the conjecture that the author calls Beilinson's (Banerjee 2502.09380, v1 Feb 2025, v2 Mar 2026), which the L-value wording of the bullet does not cover. (iv) A function-field Beilinson–Bloch criterion with unconditional special cases (Broe 2505.00696). (v) Neighbouring Bloch–Kato and Beilinson–Bloch–Kato results: Grossi–Loeffler–Zerbes (2407.17055), Kim–Pollack (2505.09121), Peng (2509.18615), and Dummigan–Golyshev–de Jeu–Kerr (2605.11100), whose Section 3 says Bloch–Kato is what fixes the rational factor in Beilinson's determinant identity; their 2-part result is therefore a statement about that factor for specific curves. (vi) Alfarano–Bianucci–Lalín–Ringeling (2608.00615, 1 Aug 2026), a Boyd Mahler-measure family, which observes the rational factors r_k numerically and proves a conditional case for k = 4u. Its Declaration of Generative AI names Anthropic's Claude (data processing and pattern identification) and Axiom's Axolver framework (training neural networks), and says the human authors directed the framework and verified all AI outputs. No other source names an AI system in connection with this problem. Close calls: (a) whether Banerjee's Albanese-kernel theorem is a restricted case of the bullet, since the authors use the same name for a different statement; (b) whether a finite set of numerical instances moves the bullet's quantity or only instantiates it (by the Collatz analogy in the instructions, instances of the universal claim should count for nothing, but the numerical checks test the regulator/L-value ratio for named varieties, which is the bullet's own quantity); (c) whether results that fix the rational factor (Dummigan et al.; Alfarano et al.) move a quantity the bullet names, since the bullet's 'up to a rational number' leaves that factor unspecified; (d) whether Claude's pattern identification in 2608.00615 is load-bearing: the paper does not say which observations it produced, and its proved statements (Lemma 3.1, Proposition 3.4) do not depend on it as far as the text read shows. The pre-window special-case literature (Borel's theorem, Boyd-type identities of Rogers–Zudilin, Mellit and Lalín, the Dokchitser–de Jeu–Zagier numerics, Kings' 2003 survey) is noted but not catalogued event by event; see incomplete.
competing_reading: Reading the bullet as the whole Beilinson circle, including Chow-group and Albanese-kernel statements, counts Banerjee (2025, v2 2026) and Gazaki–Love (2023, v3 2026) as partial progress, and Broe's function-field Beilinson–Bloch as analogue progress. Reading the bullet's own L-value wording, none of these touches its quantity. On the numerical checks: a strict reading of the universal claim treats finitely many checked curves as nothing (the Collatz analogue); a looser reading treats them as evidence about the regulator/L-value ratio, which the bullet names. On AI: a reader who takes the 'data processing' role as incidental would record Alfarano et al. as involving Claude only peripherally; a reader who takes the 'identify patterns' role as the source of the paper's observed conjectures (3-adic parity laws, p-adic distributions, Conjecture 3.2) would record Claude as load-bearing for that content, even though the paper does not say which patterns were Claude's.
what_would_settle_it: (a) The 26 January 2024 revision of the Wikipedia list, to confirm the frozen bullet wording (I read the 2026 revision, which says 'Beilinson's conjectures about special values of L-functions'). (b) The full text of arXiv 2608.00615 (PDF was unreadable; HTML read through section 6), to see which observations came from Claude's pattern identification and whether any proved statement depends on them. (c) The full text of arXiv 2502.09380 beyond Theorem 1.1 and section 2, and the introduction's definition of 'Beilinson's conjecture', to see whether the paper relates its statement to L-values. (d) The precision and method sections of arXiv 2409.19549 (sections 8 and 10), 2401.04510 (section 7), 2512.24607 (integrality assumption) and 2606.24532 (section 8), to tell whether the numerical checks are at the level of the regulator identity or only of rationality of ratios. (e) Any 2026 citing work that engages with 2502.09380, 2309.06361 or 2605.11100, or a journal decision on 2309.06361 (DOI 10.1016/j.aim.2025.110746 is listed on the arXiv page but not confirmed).
